headline: High-risk autonomous cloud workspace plus write-capable integrations create dangerous default interaction paths; the reference-only second agent limits some pairwise risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A ingests external content through GitHub, Slack, Jira, Notion, and MCP, and can act autonomously in a cloud workspace. Agent B is documentation-only and non-runnable, so it cannot inject back through tools, but its content can still be copied into A. The shared integration surfaces make prompt injection plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF operator copies B-generated text into A's workspace or tickets
IF A reads content from Slack, Notion, Jira, or MCP without provenance filtering
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of untrusted text into A
Add a provenance banner to B outputs
Require A to summarize before acting on external text
Restrict A's MCP servers to trusted sources only

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A handles source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and secrets, and has broad network egress plus write access in a cloud workspace. Agent B is local documentation-only with no filesystem or network access, so it is not a leak source, but A can still expose sensitive data into external services or copied outputs. The pair therefore creates a realistic leakage path from A to outside recipients.
conditions: IF A processes repositories containing secrets or internal chat
IF A sends workspace content to GitHub, Slack, Jira, Notion, or MCP endpoints
mitigations: Remove secrets from A's workspace before use
Limit A to least-privilege OAuth scopes
Turn off external integrations for sensitive projects
Review outbound messages from A before sending

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has broad write and git-modifying capabilities, while Agent B has no write, shell, or filesystem access. There is no overlapping mutable resource in the profiles, so direct write-write conflict is unlikely. Any conflict would require manual transfer into A, making the blast radius small and the pathway unusual.
conditions: IF operator manually copies B output into A for editing
IF A is pointed at the same repo while another writer is active
mitigations: Use branch protection on shared repos
Assign A a separate working branch
Avoid concurrent edits during A runs

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A can generate code, facts, and edits, and Agent B is a content-writing/reference agent that may render copied material. Because B has no verification or action authority, the cascade is not automatic, but A's output can still be treated as authoritative if manually transferred. The interaction exists in default documentation workflows, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF B is used to rewrite or publish A's generated text without fact-checking
IF A's outputs are copied into downstream docs or tickets
mitigations: Require human review of A-generated claims
Ask B to cite sources explicitly
Mark A outputs as untrusted until verified

E_compliance.rationale: Agent A touches team chat, issue trackers, docs, and source code and can write to SaaS integrations, which may create retention or residency mismatches if sensitive data is routed externally. Agent B is documentation-only and touches no data classes, so it adds no separate compliance burden. The main issue is A's integration footprint, not a documented cross-agent policy conflict.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into A's integrations
IF the workspace policy forbids SaaS retention for chat or issue data
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from A runs
Review retention settings on connected SaaS tools
Use separate projects for sensitive work
